analysis.title: Venture Global (VG): First Take: 3Q26 Slight Beat, Strong Raise; CP2 First LNG Production Guidance Accelerated
key_insights: VG reported 3Q26 adj. EBITDA of $2,583m, above GSe of $2,517m and FactSet consensus of $2,532m (+3%/+2%). The beat came from lower than expected O&M. Volumes and margins were in line after the October operating data pre-release.

VG raised 2026 adj. EBITDA guidance to $10.0-10.3b from $8.7-9.1b (+14% at the midpoint), above GSe/consensus of $9.03b/$9.23b. The guide assumes a $21-22/mmbtu Bal26 spot spread on the ~1% of volumes still to be sold at spot.

CP2 first LNG guidance was accelerated to mid-2027 (vs 2H27 prior and GSe of June 2027). VG also introduced 3Q27 CP2 production guidance of 10-20 cargoes (vs GSe of 16). GS says the timing of the announcement suggests its estimates could now be conservative.
Plaquemines Phase 1 reached commercial operations on 10/31 as expected, starting ~13 mtpa of Phase 1 contracts. GS expects Phase 2 COD (~7 mtpa of contracts) by June 1, 2027.

VG increased a 20-year agreement with an existing customer by 0.5 mtpa, adding to the recent ConocoPhillips and China Gas deals. Management plans to contract a large share of the remaining ~30 mtpa of uncontracted capacity, mostly through 5-year deals and some 20-year deals (potentially 5-10 mtpa). GS flags headlines that QatarEnergy is in discussion with other US LNG operators for incremental supply.

One CP1 arbitration case (Orlen) remains after the adverse Galp decision on October 8, 2026. Galp damages are capped at an aggregate $170m and will be set at a separate hearing, likely in 2027 or 2028. Aggregate pending claims are now $5.9-8.2b vs $6.1-8.4b at 2Q26. GS views this as manageable relative to cash flow.

No new details on the behind-the-meter data center power plan. The October GEV and BKR orders cover 16 x 720 MW plants supporting >10 GW of data center compute by 2034. GS sees the agreement as a low-cost call option for VG to become a large data center developer, and says holding the late 2028/early 2029 in-service timing likely requires a commercial commitment within 1H27.

GS price target and estimates are unchanged ahead of the earnings call. Buy rating, 12-month price target of $18.00 on a DCF (10.25% discount rate, 3% terminal growth), vs a $11.80 price on 9 Nov 2026 (52.5% upside).
Opex came in below GSe: O&M $303m vs $326m, G&A $113m vs $137m, development expense $33m vs $49m. Capex of $3,842m was 20.8% above GSe of $3,181m.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q26 adj. EBITDA beat GSe and consensus, 2026 EBITDA guidance was raised and CP2 first LNG timing was accelerated. GS sees a positive release and leaves its price target and estimates unchanged.

earnings_insights: VG 3Q26 reported adj. EBITDA $2,583m vs GSe $2,517m and FactSet consensus $2,532m (reported 11/10/2026), +3.7% QoQ and +69.4% YoY.
VG 3Q26 blended gross margin reported $6.46/mmbtu vs GSe ~$6.47/mmbtu. EBITDA per volume was $5.54/mmbtu, +3% above GSe.
VG 3Q26 volumes reported 466 tbtu vs GSe 466 tbtu. Cargoes reported 124 vs GSe 126.
VG 2026 adj. EBITDA guidance raised to $10.0-10.3b from $8.7-9.1b, vs GSe $9.03b and consensus $9.23b (estimates). 2026 volume guidance raised to 509-518 cargoes from 500-518, vs GSe 512.
risk_factors: CP1 arbitration is still pending (Orlen), with aggregate pending claims of $5.9-8.2b.
Execution risk on signing the incremental contracts needed for future projects.
Downside risk to global gas prices near term from a Russia/Ukraine peace agreement, and medium term from the coming wave of liquefaction projects.
Reduction in long term global LNG demand.
Project funding needs could require significant equity and/or debt raises.
Higher input costs weighing on margins.
Higher unit costs weighing on execution on excess LNG production volume realization.
geopolitical: QatarEnergy is reported to be in discussions with US LNG operators for incremental US LNG supply.
A Russia/Ukraine peace agreement is named as a near-term downside risk to global gas prices.
